name: Kitzbühel
kurzbeschreibung: The legendary city of the Hahnenkammrennen. Glamour, tradition, and breathtaking alpine scenery. Innsbruck—where the mountains meet the world.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kitzbühel is a world-renowned alpine resort town in northeastern Tyrol. The capital of the Kitzbühel district lies at an elevation of 762 metres in the wide Leukental valley along the Kitzbüheler Ache river, nestled between the striking Kitzbüheler Horn to the east and the Hahnenkamm to the west. Home to around 8,300 residents, the historic town blends glamorous mountain tourism with authentic Tyrolean heritage. Internationally celebrated as the venue for the prestigious Hahnenkamm ski races, Kitzbühel captivates visitors year-round with expansive alpine scenery, upscale boutiques, award-winning culinary establishments, and the pristine moorland waters of Lake Schwarzsee.

History

Settlement in the Kitzbühel basin dates back millennia, with copper mining established at the Kelchalm as early as 1000 BC during the Bronze Age. Bavarian tribes settled the region in the early Middle Ages, and the settlement was first documented around 1165 under the name Chizbuhel. In 1271, Duke Ludwig II of Bavaria granted Kitzbühel its town charter and fortified the settlement with sturdy town walls. Silver and copper mining brought lasting prosperity over subsequent centuries. The arrival of the Salzburg-Tyrol Railway in 1875 marked the beginning of modern alpine tourism. Skiing pioneer Franz Reisch made the first recorded ski descents on the Kitzbüheler Horn in 1893, and in 1931 the inaugural Hahnenkamm race was held, cementing Kitzbühel's status in winter sports history.

Getting There

Kitzbühel benefits from excellent transport connections. By train, the town is accessible via direct InterCity services and regional connections stopping at Kitzbühel Hauptbahnhof and Kitzbühel Hahnenkamm stations. Motorists traveling from the north follow the A12 Inntal Autobahn to the Kufstein-Süd exit, continuing along the B173, B178, and B161 Pass-Thurn road straight into town. From Salzburg, scenic routes lead through Lofer and St. Johann in Tirol. Regular regional buses operated by the Tyrol Public Transport Network connect Kitzbühel with surrounding villages and valley trailheads.

Tips

A visit to the Museum Kitzbühel, housed in the historic Pfleghof building, offers fascinating historical insights and features a renowned permanent exhibition of works by painter Alfons Walde. Winter sports enthusiasts can explore the extensive KitzSki domain featuring 233 kilometres of groomed slopes and the iconic Streif downhill course, which transforms into an educational panoramic hiking trail during summer. Hikers should ascend the Kitzbüheler Horn by cable car to discover the Alpine Flower Garden at 1,880 metres, showcasing over 400 high-altitude plant species. Lake Schwarzsee provides an idyllic spot for swimming and lakeside strolls amidst warm moorland waters.
